1	# PLAN.md: Project 2 plan (Steps 1-7)
2	
3	Author: builder agent. Status: initial version (Step 0), before review.
4	Data facts used here come from AGENTS.md. Nothing in this plan has been run yet; no result is claimed.
5	
6	## 0. Global decisions
7	
8	### Train/test split by year
9	
10	| Role | Years | Use |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| Train | 2014, 2015, 2016 | fit preprocessing and models |
13	| Tuning (only if needed) | train on 2014-2015, validate on 2016 | choose hyperparameters; then refit on 2014-2016 |
14	| Test | 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 | evaluation only; every metric is reported pooled AND per year |
15	
16	### How leakage between years is prevented
17	
18	1. One function `check_no_overlap(train_years, test_years)` (in `src/preprocess.py`) raises `ValueError` if the sets intersect. Every train/predict call in Steps 3-7 goes through it.
19	2. Every fitted object (zero-column mask, `StandardScaler`, classifiers) is fit on the training rows only. Test rows are only passed to `transform` / `predict`. `log1p` is stateless, so it cannot leak.
20	3. Tuning never touches 2017-2021.
21	4. Step 7: year t is predicted before it is used for training (see Step 7). Expanding/sliding windows refit preprocessing on the window only.
22	5. Cross-year duplicates: the 2014-2018 files have many duplicate rows and repeated apknames. Step 1 reports (a) exact duplicate feature rows within a year and (b) apknames or identical feature vectors shared between a training year and a test year. I keep all rows by default (AGENTS.md). If (b) is large, I will propose in the Step 1 report whether to drop test rows that duplicate a training row, and wait for the student's decision. I will not decide this silently.
23	6. Step 2 (KS tests, accuracy matrix) is descriptive. Its output is never used to select features, hyperparameters or the split.
24	
25	### Conventions (from AGENTS.md)
26	random_state=42; features as float32/int32; pathlib paths relative to the repo root; docstrings and type hints on every function; one module per concern; cache in a git-ignored `cache/` folder (the loader may cache the combined matrix as `.npy`); small commits tagged `[builder]`.
27	
28	### Shared constants (`src/config.py`)
29	`ROOT`, `DATA_DIR`, `RESULTS_DIR`, `DOCS_DIR`, `SEED = 42`, `TRAIN_YEARS = (2014, 2015, 2016)`, `TEST_YEARS = (2017, ..., 2021)`, `TUNE_TRAIN_YEARS = (2014, 2015)`, `TUNE_VAL_YEAR = 2016`, `N_RAW_COLUMNS = 1849`, `LABEL_COL = "label"`, `YEAR_COL = "year"`.
30	
31	### Entry point (`src/main.py`)
32	`main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`. `python -m src.main` runs Steps 1-7 in order; `--step N` (1-7) runs one step (running it first runs any earlier step it needs, using the cache). Prints a short summary, writes `results/`. Target: under about 15 minutes in total (see runtime notes per step).
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Step 1: Prepare the data (`src/data.py`)
37	
38	**Approach.** Read the 16 CSVs, take year and class only from the file name, drop `apkname`, add `label` (malware=1, benign=0) and `year`, validate the schema, and combine.
39	
40	**Functions.**
41	- `parse_filename(name: str) -> tuple[int, int]`: regex `^sampled_(\d{4})_(malware|benign)_api\.csv$` on the base name; returns `(year, label)`. Raises `ValueError` on any other name, a year outside 2014-2021, or a bad class.
42	- `list_data_files(data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR) -> list[Path]`: sorted list; raises if not exactly one malware and one benign file for each of 2014-2021 (16 files).
43	- `load_file(path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame`: reads the CSV, checks the shape is `(n, 1849)` and the first column is `apkname`, drops it, casts the 1,848 features to int32, appends `label` (int8) and `year` (int16) from `parse_filename`. Raises `ValueError` if the column count is not 1,849 or any value is negative or missing. Does not assert a row count.
44	- `read_apknames(path: Path) -> pd.Series`: the `apkname` column only (for the duplicate/overlap audit; never used as a feature).
45	- `load_year(year: int, data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR) -> pd.DataFrame`: concatenates that year's malware and benign files.
46	- `validate_feature_order(frames: list[pd.DataFrame]) -> None`: raises if any frame's feature columns differ from the first one in names or order.
47	- `combine_years(frames: dict[int, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame`: concatenates years in order (calls `validate_feature_order`); `ignore_index=True`.
48	- `load_all(data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR, use_cache: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame`: the whole dataset (~100,000 x 1,850 incl. label, year).
49	- `feature_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]`: all columns except `label` and `year` (1,848 names).
50	- `summarize_data(df: pd.DataFrame, data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR) -> pd.DataFrame`: one row per year: files loaded, rows, feature columns, malware count, benign count, exact duplicate rows, all-zero feature columns, apknames repeated within the year, and the number of rows in the year whose feature vector also occurs in an earlier year.
51	- `write_data_summary(summary: pd.DataFrame, path: Path) -> None`: Markdown + CSV.
52	
53	**Report.** `docs/step1_data_summary.md`: files per year, real row counts (not 1,500), 1,849 raw columns and 1,848 features after dropping `apkname`, malware/benign counts per year, duplicate/overlap audit, dtype and memory use. Table also saved to `results/step1_data_summary.csv`.
54	
55	**Testing.** Synthetic CSVs in `tmp_path`: `parse_filename` accepts valid names and rejects bad ones (wrong year, wrong class, extra suffix, path with directories); `load_file` drops the first column, gives 1,848 features, correct label from name, wrong column count raises; mismatched feature order raises; `combine_years` row count equals the sum of inputs; label and year columns are right. Integration test (skipped if `input_data/` is absent): 16 files, 1,849 raw columns each, 18,000 rows per year for 2014-2018 and 3,000 for 2019-2021, equal malware and benign counts, no NaN.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Step 2: Handle data drift (`src/drift.py`)
60	
61	**Approach.** Measure feature drift with the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, and check concept drift with a train-on-year-i / test-on-year-j accuracy matrix.
62	
63	**Sampling.** Every year is subsampled to the same size `n = min(rows per year)` (3,000 with the current data; computed, not hard-coded), using `random_state=42`, stratified so each sample has equal malware and benign counts. Both classes are pooled per year, so drift here includes any change in the malware/goodware mix inside a year; the balanced sampling removes that source.
64	
65	**Functions.**
66	- `subsample_years(df, n: int | None = None, seed: int = SEED) -> dict[int, pd.DataFrame]`: equal-size, class-balanced sample per year; `n=None` uses the smallest year.
67	- `ks_feature_table(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame, features: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame`: runs `scipy.stats.ks_2samp` on each feature; returns columns `feature, ks_stat, p_value, skipped`. A feature constant in both samples (same single value) is marked `skipped` (NaN stat/p) and counted, not tested.
68	- `ks_year_pairs(samples: dict[int, pd.DataFrame], features, mode: str) -> pd.DataFrame`: `mode="vs_2014"` (each year 2015-2021 vs 2014) or `mode="consecutive"` (year vs previous year). Returns one row per pair: `year_a, year_b, n_tested, n_skipped, mean_ks, share_significant`.
69	- `bonferroni_significant(p_values: np.ndarray, alpha: float = 0.05) -> np.ndarray`: boolean mask with `p < alpha / m`, `m` = number of tested (non-skipped) features.
70	- `top_drifting_features(samples, features, k: int = 20) -> pd.DataFrame`: top-k features by mean KS statistic across the "vs 2014" comparisons (also lists the per-year KS for each).
71	- `most_different_years(pair_table: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame`: pairs ranked by mean KS.
72	- `concept_drift_matrix(samples: dict[int, pd.DataFrame], features, seed: int = SEED) -> pd.DataFrame`: for each year i, fit log1p + StandardScaler + `SGDClassifier(loss="log_loss")` on year i's sample only (scaler fit on that year only), compute accuracy on every year j's sample (i==j uses a held-out 30% split of that year, so the diagonal is not training accuracy). Returns an 8x8 accuracy DataFrame.
73	- `run_drift_analysis(df) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]`: runs the above and writes `results/step2_ks_vs_2014.csv`, `step2_ks_consecutive.csv`, `step2_top20_features.csv`, `step2_accuracy_matrix.csv` and optional PNG heatmaps.
74	
75	**Runtime.** 7 + 7 year pairs x ~1,800 `ks_2samp` calls on 3,000 points is well under a minute.
76	
77	**Caveat to state in the report.** With 3,000 samples per year the KS test is very sensitive, so most features may be "significant" after Bonferroni; the mean KS statistic (effect size) is the more useful number. Features all-zero in both samples are skipped and reported as a count.
78	
79	**Report.** `docs/step2_drift_analysis.md`: method, sample size, skipped counts, table of mean KS and share significant per pair, top-20 drifting features (Dalvik signatures), which years differ most, the accuracy matrix and what it says about concept drift.
80	
81	**Testing.** Synthetic: identical samples give KS 0 and none significant; a shifted feature gives a high KS and is flagged; constant-in-both features are skipped and counted; `bonferroni_significant` uses `alpha / m` with `m` excluding skipped features (hand-computed case); `subsample_years` gives equal sizes, is reproducible with seed 42 and is class balanced; matrix is square and indexed by years; top-k returns k rows sorted descending. Real data (skipped if absent): the result tables have 7 rows each.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## Step 3: Preprocess (`src/preprocess.py`)
86	
87	**Approach.** `log1p` to tame the heavy tail (counts up to ~92,000), drop features that are all-zero in the training years, then `StandardScaler` fit on training years only. Output float32.
88	
89	**Functions.**
90	- `check_no_overlap(train_years: Iterable[int], test_years: Iterable[int]) -> None`: raises `ValueError` if they share a year (also if either is empty).
91	- `split_by_year(df, train_years, test_years) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]`: calls `check_no_overlap`, returns the train and test frames (rows selected by `year`).
92	- `apply_log1p(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray`: `np.log1p` as float32; raises on negative input.
93	- `nonzero_feature_mask(X_train: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray`: boolean mask of columns with any non-zero value in the training rows only.
94	- `class Preprocessor` (sklearn-style): `fit(X_train_raw: np.ndarray) -> Preprocessor` (applies log1p, learns the mask, fits `StandardScaler`), `transform(X_raw: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray` (log1p, mask, scale), `fit_transform`, attribute `kept_features_` (names/indices). Raises if `transform` is called before `fit`.
95	- `prepare_split(df, train_years, test_years) -> dict`: returns `X_train, y_train, years_train, X_test, y_test, years_test, preprocessor`; the preprocessor is fit on the training rows only.
96	- `make_tuning_split(df) -> dict`: same, with train 2014-2015 and validate 2016.
97	
98	**Decision flagged.** Dropping all-zero training columns is only a size reduction (such columns have zero variance and no information in training), but a column that is non-zero only in a later year is lost for the static model. That loss is real drift and is reported (count of columns active in test years but dropped). Step 7 refits the mask on each window, which recovers them.
99	
100	**Report.** `docs/step3_preprocessing.md`: log1p and why, number of columns dropped, scaler details, the split table above, and the five leakage rules.
101	
102	**Testing.** Synthetic: scaler mean/std come from training rows only (train mean ~0, std ~1; test is not centred on its own mean); the mask comes from training only (a column non-zero only in a test row is dropped); `log1p` equals `np.log1p`, negative input raises; `check_no_overlap` raises on overlap; `transform` before `fit` raises. Leakage test on the real or synthetic frame: no `year` appears in both the train and test outputs of `prepare_split`, and training years are exactly 2014-2016. Changing test rows must not change the fitted scaler (fit twice, compare `mean_`).
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Step 4: Classifiers (`src/models.py`)
107	
108	**Approach.** Three scikit-learn models, all `random_state=42`, trained on the preprocessed 2014-2016 data.
109	
110	**Functions.**
111	- `build_model(name: str) -> sklearn estimator`: `name` in `{"logreg", "random_forest", "sgd"}`; raises `ValueError` otherwise.
112	- `train_model(name: str, X_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray) -> estimator`: builds and fits.
113	- `train_all(X_train, y_train) -> dict[str, estimator]`.
114	- `tune_logreg(tune_split: dict) -> dict`: only if time allows: small grid on `C` using train 2014-2015 / validate 2016, scoring F1 (malware); returns best params and the grid scores.
115	- `MODEL_NAMES: tuple[str, ...]`.
116	
117	**Models and hyperparameter justification.**
118	- `LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced", max_iter=1000, solver="lbfgs", C=1.0, random_state=42)`: linear baseline that works well on scaled sparse-ish counts; `balanced` protects against label imbalance if present (the data is balanced per year, but later use may not be); `max_iter=1000` so lbfgs converges on ~1,000 standardized features (a `ConvergenceWarning` is treated as a problem to report); `C=1.0` is the default, changed only if tuning on 2016 says so.
119	- `RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, n_jobs=-1, random_state=42)`: non-linear model that is insensitive to feature scale; 200 trees is a point where accuracy usually plateaus while training stays within a minute or two on ~54,000 rows; other settings default (unbounded depth, `max_features="sqrt"`).
120	- `SGDClassifier(loss="log_loss", penalty="l2", alpha=1e-4, class_weight="balanced", max_iter=1000, tol=1e-3, random_state=42)`: a logistic model trained by SGD, needed because Step 7 uses `partial_fit` (LogisticRegression and RandomForest have none). `alpha=1e-4` is the sklearn default and a standard regularisation level for ~50k samples. For `partial_fit` the first call passes `classes=[0, 1]`.
121	
122	**Report.** `docs/step4_models.md`: the three models, why each, the hyperparameter table and justification, training time per model, any convergence warnings, and tuning results if run.
123	
124	**Testing.** Synthetic separable data: each model trains and predicts both classes with accuracy above chance (e.g. > 0.9); `build_model` returns the right class with `random_state == 42` (and `class_weight == "balanced"`, `n_estimators == 200` where applicable); unknown name raises; SGD has `partial_fit`; same seed gives identical predictions twice; training with rows from a test year raises (guard checked via `years_train` argument in `train_all_from_split`, see below). A test that the training matrix has only years 2014-2016.
125	- `train_all_from_split(split: dict) -> dict[str, estimator]`: wraps `train_all` and asserts `set(split["years_train"]) <= set(TRAIN_YEARS)`.
126	
127	---
128	
129	## Steps 5 and 6: Evaluation (`src/evaluate.py`)
130	
131	**Approach.** Predict on held-out test years 2017-2021 only. Malware (1) is the positive class. Step 5 is the pooled table; Step 6 is the per-year breakdown.
132	
133	**Functions.**
134	- `compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]`: `accuracy, precision, recall, f1`, using `pos_label=1`, `zero_division=0`.
135	- `evaluate_model(model, X_test, y_test) -> dict[str, float]`.
136	- `pooled_table(models: dict, X_test, y_test) -> pd.DataFrame`: one row per classifier, columns `model, accuracy, precision, recall, f1, n_test` (Step 5; pooled over 2017-2021).
137	- `per_year_table(models: dict, X_test, y_test, years_test) -> pd.DataFrame`: one row per (model, year), same metrics plus `year, n`; only years in `TEST_YEARS` (Step 6).
138	- `drift_summary(per_year: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame`: per model: first-test-year F1, last-test-year F1, drop, and the F1 slope across years.
139	- `assert_test_years_only(years: np.ndarray) -> None`: raises if any year is outside `TEST_YEARS`.
140	- `save_table(df: pd.DataFrame, stem: str) -> None`: writes `results/<stem>.csv` and `results/<stem>.md` (Markdown table with fixed rounding to 4 decimals).
141	- `run_evaluation(df) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]`: runs Steps 3-4 pipeline, writes `results/step5_pooled_metrics.*`, `results/step6_per_year_metrics.*`, optional `results/step6_f1_by_year.png`.
142	
143	**Notes.** Pooled metrics weight years by size (2017-2018 are 6x larger than 2019-2021), so the per-year table is the primary view; the report says so.
144	
145	**Reports.** `docs/step5_evaluation.md` (pooled table, accuracy as the primary metric, plus precision/recall/F1 and a short comparison). `docs/step6_test_results.md` (per-year table for each classifier, how performance changes as data drifts, link to Step 2 findings).
146	
147	**Testing.** Hand-computed confusion matrix (e.g. TP=3, FP=1, FN=2, TN=4) gives the exact accuracy, precision, recall and F1; metrics treat 1 as positive (swapping labels changes precision/recall); all-benign predictions give recall 0 and precision 0 without raising; `per_year_table` has one row per model per test year, the row counts `n` sum to the pooled `n_test`, and weighted per-year accuracy equals the pooled accuracy; `assert_test_years_only` raises on a training year; files are written with the expected columns.
148	
149	---
150	
151	## Step 7: Sustainable approach (`src/sustainable.py`)
152	
153	**Approach.** Compare four strategies on the same test years (2017-2021), same metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1; malware positive), reported per year and pooled. Rule for all of them: year t is predicted before any of its rows is used for training or for fitting preprocessing.
154	
155	| Strategy | Training data used to predict year t |
156	|---|---|
157	| (a) static | 2014-2016 only, never updated (this is the Step 4/6 model) |
158	| (b) expanding window | all years before t (2014..t-1); preprocessing and model refit from scratch for each t |
159	| (c) sliding window | the 3 years before t (t-3..t-1); preprocessing and model refit for each t |
160	| (d) incremental | SGD fit on 2014-2016, then for t = 2017..2021: predict t, then `partial_fit` on t (test-then-train) |
161	
162	For t=2017 the windows in (b) and (c) are both 2014-2016, so (a)-(c) agree on 2017; they differ from 2018 on.
163	
164	**Functions.**
165	- `window_years(strategy: str, t: int) -> tuple[int, ...]`: training years for strategy `"static"`, `"expanding"` or `"sliding"` at test year t (static: 2014-2016; expanding: 2014..t-1; sliding: t-3..t-1); raises if t is not in `TEST_YEARS` or if any returned year is >= t.
166	- `run_window_strategy(df, strategy: str, model_name: str = "logreg") -> pd.DataFrame`: for each t: `check_no_overlap(window, [t])`, fit a new `Preprocessor` and model on the window only, predict t, compute metrics; returns one row per test year.
167	- `run_incremental(df, model_name: str = "sgd") -> pd.DataFrame`: initial `fit` of `Preprocessor` and SGD on 2014-2016 (preprocessor frozen afterwards, so later years use the same mask and scaler: a limitation noted in the report); loop over t, record the prediction on t first, then `partial_fit` on year t with the true labels. Returns one row per test year.
168	- `run_all_strategies(df) -> pd.DataFrame`: concatenates (a)-(d) with a `strategy` column, adds a pooled row per strategy.
169	- `compare_to_static(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame`: per strategy and year, difference in F1 and accuracy against the static model.
170	- `run_sustainable(df) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]`: writes `results/step7_strategy_metrics.*`, `results/step7_vs_static.*`, optional `results/step7_f1_by_year.png`.
171	
172	**Model choice and decision flagged.** Windows (b)-(c) and the static baseline use LogisticRegression so that all five refits finish in a few minutes; (d) uses SGD. A fair isolation of "incremental vs retrain" would also run SGD under (a)-(c); I will add SGD-static as an extra row (cheap) so the incremental gain is compared with the same model family. RandomForest under (b)/(c) is run only if the total time stays below the 15-minute budget; otherwise stated as skipped. Runtime estimate: ~54,000-90,000 rows x ~1,000 features per LR refit, 5 refits per strategy; to be measured, not assumed.
173	
174	**Assumption to state.** Labels for year t become available only after year t ends (test-then-train); a real labeling delay would hurt (d), (b) and (c) in practice. The report states this. Not simulated here.
175	
176	**Report.** `docs/step7_sustainable_approach.md`: the four strategies, the table of F1/accuracy per year, comparison with the static model, cost (training time per strategy), conclusions that feed the one-page report.
177	
178	**Testing.** Synthetic multi-year frame with an injected drift (class boundary shifts each year): `window_years` returns exactly the specified years (including edge cases t=2017 and t=2021); for every strategy and every t, `max(window) < t` (the no-test-year-in-training check, run through a spy that records the years passed to `fit`); `run_incremental` records predictions on t before `partial_fit` on t (verified with a stub model that logs call order and, separately, by checking the year-t labels are not seen at prediction time); static results are identical to the Step 6 model's results; result tables have one row per test year per strategy and the expected columns; on the injected-drift data the retraining/incremental strategies do not do worse than the static one in the final year (sanity check, not a performance claim).
179	
180	---
181	
182	## Cross-cutting test plan (tester)
183	- `tests/test_stepN_*.py` per step with synthetic data in `tmp_path`; real-data tests marked and skipped when `input_data/` is absent.
184	- A project-wide leakage test: every call that fits anything records the years it saw (via a spy/wrapper); none of 2017-2021 may appear before its own prediction.
185	- `python harness.py test N` for one step and `python harness.py test all` for all.
186	
187	## Implementation order and commits
188	One commit per task (about 300 added lines max): config + data, then drift, then preprocess, then models, then evaluate, then sustainable, then main and docs. Each step is followed by a review and test cycle outside this plan.
189	
190	## Points where I disagree or want a decision
191	1. The accuracy matrix in Step 2 trains on later years and predicts earlier ones; this is a diagnostic only, not used for any design choice.
192	2. Step 7 (d) freezes the scaler and zero-column mask from 2014-2016; an alternative (updating the scaler with `partial_fit`) is possible but not planned.
193	3. Cross-year duplicate handling (item 5 above) is left for the student to decide after the Step 1 audit.

I revised PLAN.md for every Accepted comment (1–9 and 11) and skipped comment 10, which was Rejected. I only edited PLAN.md, and I wrote no project code. Nothing was run, so no results are claimed. I also added a "Changes after review" section to PLAN.md.

| Comment | What changed | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SGD no longer uses `class_weight`. The Step 4 test must now call `partial_fit` on the model `build_model("sgd")` returns. | 879dfa9 |
| 2 | Section 0 now says `concept_drift_matrix` fits on single years, nothing from it feeds Steps 3–7, and the leakage tests skip `drift.py`. I also updated the "Points where I disagree" list and the cross-cutting test plan to match. | 84dffaf |
| 3 | `MIN_SUPPORT = 10`: keep only columns non-zero in at least 10 training rows. The plan adds a near-constant-column test (9 rows dropped, 10 kept) and notes the rule in the Step 3 report. | 0faea94 |
| 4 | Step 1 gets a new `train_duplicate_mask` function and reports how many test rows duplicate a training row. Steps 5 and 6 get a new `sensitivity_tables` function that reports metrics on test rows with no training duplicate. Main results keep all rows. | 3472140 |
| 5 | `check_no_overlap` now also requires `max(train_years) < min(test_years)`. The Step 2 matrix is exempt, and the plan adds a test for train 2018–2020 / test 2014. | 84dffaf |
| 6 | The cache is keyed on file names, sizes, mtimes and a schema version, and stored in the git-ignored `cache/` folder. It saves the column names, reruns the schema checks on load, and is dropped if it gets complicated. This adds a `cache_key` function and cache tests. | ffcaab2 |
| 7 | `train_all_from_split` moved into the Step 4 function list as the static 2014–2016 guard. Step 7 uses `window_years` plus `check_no_overlap` instead. | 6e83b81 |
| 8 | The Step 7 report must note the row-count imbalance and list each window's year composition. It is also saved as `results/step7_window_composition.csv`. No equal-rows variant. | 5f40832 |
| 9 | One-sentence caveat in the Step 2 report that duplicates and ties inflate KS p-values, so the KS statistic is the main signal. Subsampling is unchanged. | 5f40832 |
| 10 | Rejected, so no change. | n/a |
| 11 | `list_data_files` runs `parse_filename` on every CSV, so a stray file raises. The plan adds a stray-file test. | 6e83b81 |

I combined 2 with 5 and 7 with 11, and 8 with 9 and the new section, because those edits touch the same passages. Each of those pairs therefore shares a commit hash. Every commit message carries the comment numbers.

Nothing is left unfinished. Comment 1 still rests on the reviewer's and the student's knowledge of sklearn, since sklearn isn't installed on this machine. Re-confirm it once the environment is set up.
